problem:
Express $7\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)$ in the form $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-ϕ)$ with $ϕ\in (0,\frac{\pi }{2}).$ Use the **exact value** for $R,$ and round $ϕ$ to **three decimal places**.

$7\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,≈\,$
{{field-1}}
$\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x\,-$
{{field-2}}$)$
worked_solution:
The difference formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
7\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
7\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x).
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=7 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{7} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{7} \\ ϕ & =arctan\,(\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{7})≈0.460\text{ }\text{rad},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)^{2}+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2} & ={7}^{2}+(2\sqrt{3})^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =49+12 \\ {R}^{2} & =61 \\ R & =\sqrt{61}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
7\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)≈\sqrt{61}\,sin\,(3x-0.460).
$$
